title: Disconnected Deploy Toolkit — TF interfaces, artifact catalog, and mirror strategy
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working draft for a compact "disconnected deploy" toolkit focused on: artifact mirroring, offline registries, curated dependency bundles, and the Terraform module surface we expect customers/operators to consume. The audience is engineering (solutions + infra) and professional services prepping private/VPC and on-prem installs for air-gapped environments.

Goal: give a minimal, repeatable sequence for provisioning an air-gapped Redwood Private deployment and for performing non-disruptive upgrades. Emphasis on reproducible artifact catalogs, integrity checks, and clear TF inputs so installs can be automated or run with a runbook.

High-level approach (one-liner):
- Produce a self-contained bundle (tar.gz) that contains: image/OCI layers, helm charts, operator binaries, base OS packages (apt/rpm), model weights (optionally), and a JSON manifest with checksums and provenance.
- Host the bundle on an offline registry (registry mirror + filesystem layout) consumed by the customer's local registry proxy or on-prem registry appliance.
- Provide a Terraform module that exposes simple hooks: where to point the registry, credentials, and bundle metadata; module handles k8s manifests, imagePullSecrets wiring, and ensuring node-level prerequisites.

Quick checklist (install runbook summary):
1) Validate pre-requisites on target environment: supported k8s version, container runtime compatibility, available GPU drivers (if using GPU), storageclass present, NTP, customer KMS accessible (or fallback).
2) Transfer bundle.tar.gz to the air-gapped site (SCP / physical media).
3) Verify manifest signatures and checksums (see verification commands below).
4) Unpack bundle onto the offline registry host; run mirror import script to populate the local registry and package cache.
5) Run the Terraform module with minimal inputs (registry endpoint, TLS certs, credentials) to bootstrap infra layer + namespaces + CRDs.
6) Apply k8s operator/helm chart from the local registry.
7) Smoke-tests: health probes, sample inference request, KV cache warming.
8) If upgrade: follow upgrade flow (section later) with canary target and rollback plan.

Bundle composition (recommended minimal layout):
- /bundle/manifest.json  -- human + machine readable list of artifacts with sha256 and type (image, chart, package, model).
- /bundle/containers/  -- tarballs or oci-layout directory of images (oci copy format) or a registry export (skopeo dir or crane export).
- /bundle/charts/  -- helm chart tgzs with values-templates.
- /bundle/packages/  -- OS packages (rpm/dpkg) or a list of downloadable checksums for offline mirrors.
- /bundle/models/  -- optional weights, or pointers to a separate model bundle protected by customer policy.
- /bundle/scripts/import-*  -- import scripts for major registry types (Harbor, NexusDocker, Artifactory, local docker/distribution).
- /bundle/signature.sig  -- detached signature (cosign or GPG) with signer identity and timestamp.

Manifest example fields (must be present):
- artifact_id: string (semantic id: redwood/serving-runtime:1.6.0)
- artifact_type: image|chart|package|model|file
- source_uri: original upstream uri
- sha256: checksum string
- size_bytes: string (for transfer planning)
- platform: linux/amd64, linux/ppc64le, etc.

Verification commands (examples to include in runbook):
- sha256sum manifest.json && jq -r '.artifacts[].sha256' manifest.json | xargs -n1 sha256sum -c --quiet
- cosign verify-blob --key <public.pem> --signature signature.sig manifest.json
- skopeo inspect --raw dir://./containers/<image> | jq -r '.config.digest'  # local validation after import

Terraform module interface (notes + recommended variables):
- Module name: redwood/private-airgap
- Required inputs (minimal):
  - registry_endpoint (string)  -- e.g., https://local-registry.internal:5000
  - registry_ca_pem (string) -- PEM content for the registry TLS cert (or path if using remote state)
  - registry_admin_user (string)
  - registry_admin_password_secret_id (string)  -- reference to vault or KMS secret name, prefer secure secret manager, but allow plaintext for initial bootstrap as last resort
  - bundle_manifest_path (string) -- local path on runner machine (makes terraform apply idempotent if content hashed)
  - cluster_context (string) -- kubecontext for apply-time commands
  - install_namespace (string) -- default "redwood-system"
  - enable_gpu_nodes (bool) -- default false; triggers nodeSelector and device-plugin Helm values

- Optional/advanced inputs:
  - import_timeout (string) -- time for registry import job e.g., "60m"
  - crd_wait_timeout (string) -- wait for CRDs created by helm to be established
  - pre_pull_images (bool) -- trigger Kubernetes DaemonSet to pre-pull images to nodes as part of apply

- Outputs (suggested):
  - controller_service_url (string)
  - bundle_applied_hash (string) -- sha256 of bundle manifest used for telemetry
  - registry_import_job_id (string)

Implementation notes for TF module:
- Keep heavy operations outside of core Terraform state where possible. TF should orchestrate a small import job (k8s Job) that returns success/failure; do not capture large blobs in TF state. Use external data sources to compute bundle hash and pass it as a simple string.
- Use local-exec sparingly; prefer k8s_job resource to run import tooling inside the cluster or on a designated import host. This avoids depending on workstation env.
- Provide a `dry_run` mode which validates manifest and simulates import without pushing images (useful for auditors).
- Expose a `post_install_scripts` variable (list of strings) which are executed by the import Job; ensures site-specific glue can run (e.g., loading CA into cluster nodes).

Upgrade plan (safe path):
- Versioning: expect bundles to be versioned: v1.6.0 -> v1.7.0. Each bundle must include a compatibility table in manifest that states minimum k8s version, operator CRD schema version, and database migration steps (if any).
- Canary upgrade flow (air-gapped):
  1) Prepare v1.7.0 bundle and import into registry under a canary tag (redwood/serving-runtime:1.7.0-canary).
  2) Terraform apply with `canary_selector` to create a canary Deployment with small replica count (one or two) wired to the new image tag.
  3) Run smoke tests and baseline performance tests (latency p50/p95, token/sec for typical prompt).
  4) If metrics within SLOs, promote canary by retagging images in the local registry (or by updating helm values) and rolling out to full replica set.
  5) If failure, revert canary by deleting canary deployment and leaving stable tags untouched.

Rollback considerations:
- Keep last-known-good bundle available locally (do not prune registry until 30 days after upgrade).
- Maintain DB schema backward-compatibility where possible. If migration is irreversible, require offline backup and restore playbook to be run prior to upgrade.

Testing and validation matrix (minimum tests to automate):
- Import validation: manifest checksum, signature, and sample skopeo pull of critical images.
- Helm/CRD validation: `helm template` + `kubectl apply --server-dry-run=client` to verify manifests render locally with provided values.
- Runtime smoke tests: health endpoints, a 5-request inference scenario, and a simple embedding call.
- Performance baseline: run 30s token generation at typical prompt size and assert expected throughput delta vs stable baseline.

Common pitfalls and notes from past installs (lessons learned):
- Customers often have older container runtimes that reject newer image manifest formats (manifest v2 schema 2 vs OCI). Provide both OCI and docker-archive exports in bundle to maximize compatibility.
- Registry TLS: customers sometimes bring a TLS-intercepting proxy. Recommend documenting exact CA pinning steps and provide an automated script to insert the registry CA into the node's OS trust store and container runtime trust store.
- CRD/helm ordering: CRDs must be applied before chart install if CRD creation is skipped by Helm. Our TF module should ensure CRDs are created and established first.
- Large image transfers: recommend rsync with checksum verification or physical disk if >150GB. Provide an estimator script in the bundle to compute expected total size.

TODOs / open questions:
- Model weights: should these ship inside the same bundle or as a separate model bundle with stricter signing? Need PS input on customer expectations. (action: @Miguel to propose model bundle policy)
- Long-term retention: propose default registry pruning policy of 90 days for snapshots, but for upgrades keep at least two versions for 30 days. Need legal input for retention when models contain customer data.
- Integration with customer vault/KMS: our TF module exposes a `secret_id` input, but we need a recommended pattern for on-prem vault init (init script in bundle?).

Appendix: Sample import command snippets (for runbook copy/paste)
- On import host (docker/distribution style):
  mkdir /opt/redwood-import && tar xzf bundle.tar.gz -C /opt/redwood-import
  cd /opt/redwood-import/containers
  for f in *.tar; do docker load -i $f && docker tag $(docker images --format '{{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}}' | head -n1) local-registry.internal:5000/${f%.tar} && docker push local-registry.internal:5000/${f%.tar}; done

- With skopeo dir export (preferred for reproducibility):
  skopeo copy --insecure-policy dir://./containers/ oci://local-registry.internal:5000 --dest-tls-verify=false

- Helm install (example):
  helm repo add redwood-local https://local-registry.internal:8443/charts
  helm install redwood-controller redwood-local/redwood-controller --namespace redwood-system --create-namespace --values ./charts/values-production.yaml

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc short and put long-form TF patterns in a dedicated module README under github PR. Drive doc should be a runbook + quick reference; link to PR for code.
- After next install, copy failure notes into this doc (network quirks, paths, cert problems).

References and links:
- Slack: #private-deploy-installs channel (search thread "Airgap March 2024")
- Github: github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/tree/main/modules/airgap-import
- Confluence: confluence.redwood/workspaces/PD-AIRGAP (design notes)

End of draft — feedback welcome.
